knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Current ratio equals current assets divided by current liabilities: 40,000 divided by 20,000 is 2.0.
Falling gross margin with unchanged sales points first to direct costs or discounts, which are checked before any other cause.
Ratio thresholds are rules of thumb that prompt questions. They are not legal tests, and no Australian trade benchmark has been checked.

practicalCriteria: Learner works out gross margin, the margin left after all costs, current ratio, debt to equity and receivable days, each with its numerator, denominator, period and formula
Each ratio has one sentence of meaning and one question, with no conclusion beyond the figures
Learner proposes a first action for the weakest ratio, and explains why a price cut is not the first response to slow payment
No threshold is presented as a legal test or an Australian benchmark
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed working document for the lesson, saved with its formulas or calculation notes
Knowledge check result (a quiz result is not a practical competence result)
stopWorkCriteria: Do not use ratios for lending or investment decisions until the tax treatment is checked
Stop and escalate any threshold used as a benchmark without a checked source
Do not change prices as the first response to slow payment without checking invoicing first
